name: ml-competition-ai-rules-census
made_by: MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents working in his name
method: For each platform or contest the platform-wide terms page (or, where none exists, the standard per-competition rules template or the platform's own documentation) was fetched on 2026-10-17 and searched for: AI-assisted or AI-generated code; AutoML; commercial LLM APIs inside a solution; external data; pre-trained models; whether companies or legal entities may enter; age and sanctions; winner code terms; reproducibility audits. Quotes are verbatim fragments of at most 125 characters each. 'read_how' says whether the primary page was read directly, read from a saved copy, or only seen through search-result snippets. On 2026-10-18 EvalAI's public JSON list of running challenges (https://eval.ai/api/challenges/challenge/present/approved/public, 18 challenges; the upcoming list https://eval.ai/api/challenges/challenge/future/approved/public was empty) was searched in every field for placeholder text ('Lorem', 'ipsum', 'consectetur', 'dolor sit'), in the terms fields for AI-tool terms, and its has_prize flags were counted; the challenges that stood out were re-read from https://eval.ai/api/challenges/challenge/<id>. On 2026-10-21 Zindi's public competition list (https://api.zindi.world/v1/competitions, first page of 20, 7 open of 515 listed) was taken, and the JSON of all 7 open competitions plus 2 recently closed ones was fetched from https://api.zindi.world/v1/competitions/<slug> and searched for LLM coding tools, development assistants, AI tools, generative AI, ChatGPT, AutoML, paid APIs, proprietary model services and disclosure of AI use; the platform rules page https://zindi.world/rules was re-fetched the same day. Also on 2026-10-21 the ARC Prize 2026 overview page was fetched and added as a contest record. Long JSON pages were read by a text-extraction model in parts of 100,000 characters.
headline: No platform-wide terms of 12 platforms or contests read have a clause on AI-assisted or AI-generated code. Clauses exist only at competition level, and two have now been found. The first explicit PERMISSION is in one Zindi competition: the Bias Bounty Mapping Equity Challenge (rules updated 2026-10-06) says commercial LLM coding tools may be used for drafting, debugging, testing and documentation, provided the submitted solution does not need them to run or reproduce. It is 1 of the 7 open Zindi competitions on 2026-10-21; the other 6 use Zindi's standard text, which says only open-source languages and tools may be used 'in building models' and does not separate a coding assistant from a modelling tool. The other clause (eBay 2026 University ML Competition - Canada, on EvalAI) restricts data and output licensing, not authorship. The rules that otherwise bind an AI-made entry stay indirect: natural-person-only eligibility (DrivenData, Kaggle), open-source / no-paid-service / no-internet rules that keep commercial LLM APIs out of the solution itself (Zindi, bitgrit, ARC Prize 2026 on Kaggle), and reproducibility audits (NeurIPS EEG/EMG 2026, bitgrit, Zindi).

changes.what: Zindi competition-level check: all 7 open competitions plus 2 recently closed ones. One (bias-bounty-mapping-equity-challenge) has the first explicit clause found that permits AI-assisted code: commercial LLM coding tools allowed for drafting, debugging, testing and documentation if the solution does not depend on them. The other 8 carry Zindi's standard text ('You may only use open-source languages and tools in building models for this challenge.') and no AI-tool clause. Zindi's platform rules page re-fetched: still no AI-tool clause. Added ARC Prize 2026 (no internet in Kaggle evaluation, so no GPT/Claude API inside a solution; prize code must be open source under CC0 or MIT-0). Headline rewritten: '0 clauses' now holds for platform-wide terms only.

Checked all 18 running public EvalAI challenges: none ships the starter template's Lorem ipsum terms; none has has_prize true, though one (id 2672) lists $1,500 in cash prizes in its description while its terms say 'There are no prizes.' and its API end_date (2099) disagrees with its stated deadline (May 31, 2026); one (id 2680, eBay, Canadian students) has an explicit 'Use of AI' section about data and licensing.

Added EvalAI (host documentation and starter template) and CrunchDAO (documentation landing page). Re-tried Numerai, Signate, Topcoder and HeroX: their terms pages were JS-only, redirected or missing, so they stay under not_covered with the reason.
First census: Zindi, AIcrowd, DrivenData, Kaggle, Codabench, NeurIPS 2026 EEG/EMG Foundation Challenge, Wunder Fund Alfa Connectome, ThinkOnward, bitgrit.

platforms.external_data: Unless stated, no external data sets are allowed in Zindi competitions.

platforms.reproducibility: Code requested from top 10 within 48 h; 'If your code does not run you will be dropped from the top 20.' 'Always set the seed.'

limits: Platform terms were read on one date (2026-10-17), EvalAI's live list one day later, and Zindi's competitions and ARC Prize 2026 on 2026-10-21. Rules change; per-competition rules can override every platform-wide term quoted here.
Kaggle quotes come from search-result snippets of rules pages, not from a direct read; Kaggle's pages are JS-rendered.

The EvalAI and CrunchDAO records rest on documentation pages, not on binding terms: EvalAI has no platform-wide participation terms, and CrunchDAO's per-competition rules were not read. The ARC Prize record rests on the overview page, not on each track's detailed rules.

The EvalAI live check covers only challenges in the public 'present/approved' list on 2026-10-18; private, unapproved and past challenges were not checked. The long JSON list was read in two parts by a text-search model, and the three challenges discussed (2266, 2672, 2680) were re-read one by one.

The Zindi check covers the 7 open competitions and 2 closed ones, not Zindi's 515 listed competitions. Three of the long competition JSON pages were read only to 100,000 characters; the unread rest held repeated copies of parent-competition rules. The JSON was read by a text-extraction model, not parsed by code.
Quotes are fragments of at most 125 characters, so some sentences are split; the URL gives the full text.

Absence of a clause is reported as 'not addressed', never as 'allowed'. Whether Zindi reads its standard 'open-source languages and tools in building models' sentence as covering coding assistants is not known; only the organisers can say.
